newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Kabul accuses UNHCR employees of hostile acts.
newsitem.headline: Kabul accuses UNHCR employees of hostile acts.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia on Thursday accused detained local employees of the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR of engaging in hostile acts, according to a Pakistan-based Afghan news service.
A Taleban spokesman, quoted by the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP), also said the arrested UNHCR employees would be released if found innocent but would be punished if found guilty.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said on Wednesday it was suspending most of its relief operations in Kabul in protest at what it said were arrests and intimidation of its staff by the Taleban.

Four of the 22 local staff in the UNHCR's main office in Kabul had been arrested, while seven Afghan women employees had been told to stay at home since the Islamic Taleban movement captured Kabul on September 27, a UNHCR official said.

Taleban deputy foreign minister Sher Mohammad Stanakzai told a senior U.N. official, Francis Okela, in Kabul on Thursday that some local UNHCR employees had used the UNHCR radio to pass military information to opposition forces, AIP said, quoting the official Kabul radio.
A spokesman of the Pakistan Foreign Ministry said earlier Islamabad could help the UNHCR sort out its problems with the Taleban if asked to do so.
The virtual suspension of UNHCR activities coincided with the start of a vital winter relief programme for Kabul.
The agency said that effective security guarantees are lacking, despite assurances given by the Taleban authorities.

AIP quoted the Taleban spokesman in the southern Afghan town of Kandahar, Wakil Ahmad, as urging the UNHCR to resume its suspended activities and saying that the Taleban government would provide full protection to UNHCR establishments.
